Approved generated-equation reliability target and preservation boundary.

verification: npx playwright test focused solve-x reader, editor parity, and dev-review cohorts
allowedWork: Solve-x reader exemplar, shared typed presentation selection, equation DOM material motion, dev-review capture lifecycle, reader masthead and TOC, focused tests, durable visual checks, and one verified commit per slice.
Preserve semantic math, searchable prose, URL routing, scroll authority, rewind, static and no-JS output, KaTeX typography identity, and production exclusion of dev review tooling.
disallowedWork: Do not generalize recipes to generated families, other subjects, editor families, graphs, code, flashcards, or providers before the final human checkpoint.
Do not use WebGL for equation glyph motion, change mathematical content, add public review infrastructure, upload logs, or convert review notes into Theseus work automatically.
goal: Restore canonical motion clarity in the solve-x reader, repair per-note review capture, prove endpoint continuity, add coherent depth and navigation affordances, and stop for human approval before generalization.
commitCadence: Commit after each independently verified slice and Theseus workspace validation.
stopConditions: Stop immediately if semantic math, searchable prose, URL restoration, scroll or rewind authority, static output, KaTeX identity, or production exclusion regresses.
Stop at s16 and s19 only if automated visual metrics expose unresolved discontinuity; retain the exemplar rollback unit.
Stop after s27 for explicit human visual approval before any generalization.
Stop if work requires WebGL glyph motion, public review infrastructure, family-wide promotion, or scope outside the approved exemplar.

slices.title: Failed review contract
slices.summary: Recorded the rejected human checkpoint and created a typed, advance-approved 27-slice exemplar repair contract with one-commit cadence, broad gates, composable motion scope, independent rollback, and mandatory human promotion stop.

slices.title: Per-note capture lifecycle
slices.summary: Each note now locks a fresh frame on first meaningful input, releases it only after durable success, preserves it across failed retries, and isolates obsolete asynchronous captures across close/reopen.

slices.title: Capture lock and retake UI
slices.summary: The composer visibly identifies a locked note moment, exposes checkpoint/progress/phase/route, supports draft-preserving retake and capture retry, and retains canonical focus and narrow-viewport behavior.

slices.title: Review workflow browser proof
slices.summary: Proved on the real solve-x reader that two notes submitted without closing the panel capture distinct current reader moments, retain route/build/render evidence, increment the inbox counter, and do not move the lesson during note capture or submission.

slices.title: Typed presentation profile
slices.summary: Added an immutable typed equation presentation profile that independently selects trajectory, cancellation, zero witness, successor, and depth recipes; validates unknown metadata; and preserves the editor's current compatibility flags.

slices.title: Reader profile authority
slices.summary: Made the shared presentation profile authoritative in the solve-x reader, exposed every selected recipe for diagnostics, and prevented canonical continuity assets from silently enabling legacy witnessed-annihilation or successor-synthesis motifs.

slices.title: Cross-surface frame contract
slices.summary: Added a strict immutable cross-surface equation frame that preserves semantic fragment identity, ownership, opacity, typography evidence, and both pixel and normalized geometry so editor and reader can be compared without sharing DOM implementation.

slices.title: Canonical parity browser gate
slices.summary: Added a browser parity gate that compares canonical editor and reader cancellation/final frames by semantic role and normalized geometry, verifies shared continuity profile and KaTeX identity, explicitly detects the current oversized reader type, and corrected visual capture to use the equation viewport.

slices.title: Native endpoint laws
slices.summary: Defined and tested a neutral native-endpoint law covering exact source/target progress, exclusive native authority, complete material/counterpart release, absent one-sided endpoints, and bounded geometry residual with typed diagnostics.

slices.title: Alignment path repair
slices.summary: Repaired alignment by keeping native source/target bounds exact, applying bounded perceptual correction only through a reversible endpoint-zero path envelope, propagating direction explicitly, and sharing one fit transform across the full solve-x sequence; visible relation ink now crosses both phase boundaries below the 2px gate.

slices.title: Native handoff continuity
slices.summary: Integrated native-endpoint law evidence into the reader, made progress 0/1000 exact despite sub-permille physical scroll residuals, and proved source/final native ink has exclusive authority, zero material visibility, and at most 0.5px planned geometry residual.

slices.title: Phase boundary and rewind continuity
slices.summary: Exposed reader playback direction and proved with the real physical scroll clock that forward then reverse traversal across both phase boundaries returns visible relation ink to the same subpixel pose and opacity while retaining the same persistent material-owner DOM node.

slices.title: Equation typography scale
slices.summary: Replaced oversized reader equation clamps with one responsive canonical type token used by native measurement, material clones, static/no-JS output, and mobile; browser gate now enforces 0.99–1.01 editor parity.

slices.title: Counter-orbit cancellation recipe
slices.summary: Added a typed, profile-selected counter-orbit recipe shared by editor and reader: inverse terms follow symmetric opposing arcs, return to baseline before fade, and survivor compaction waits until cancellation clears so x is never crossed.

slices.title: Independent zero witness
slices.summary: Added a renderer-neutral independent +0 witness with its own immutable plan, DOM identity, KaTeX rendering, readable dwell, and shared editor-reader timing; visual capture now proves cancelling terms fully clear before +0 appears and +0 clears before compaction.

slices.title: Cancellation visual gate
slices.summary: Added a durable rendered cancellation gate across wide/narrow viewports and dense forward/rewind samples; it proves protected-symbol clearance, bounded adjacent travel and opacity, exclusive term/+0/compaction phases, KaTeX parity, and cross-surface placement, while fixing a 9.7px heading-reflow jerk and undersized editor +0.

slices.title: Successor convergence recipe
slices.summary: Added convergence-v1 shared by editor and reader. The ordered 7 minus 3 expression compresses on one baseline, while 4 remains absent until later native handoff. Gold review vocabulary now names successor convergence.

slices.title: Catalyst and target gating
slices.summary: Convergence now reads authored material-input and catalyst roles without enabling successor synthesis. The minus catalyst retires first, operands remain legible longer, and the result cannot appear until every merge source is absent.

slices.title: Successor visual gate
slices.summary: Added a durable wide and narrow successor gate covering semantic ordering, baseline stability, protected-symbol clearance, overflow, KaTeX identity, exclusive source-target phases, bounded adjacent motion and opacity, and exact rewind. The gate found and repaired an overly abrupt fade window.

slices.title: Depth envelope contract
slices.summary: Defined a renderer-neutral semantic-depth-v1 envelope with bounded transform and shadow values, exact flat endpoints, deterministic rewind, progress clamping, and no authority over opacity, ownership, measurement, or layout.

slices.title: KaTeX depth presentation
slices.summary: Enabled semantic-depth-v1 for the canonical solve-x asset and applied the bounded lift only to active KaTeX relation fragments. Editor and reader share elevation, transform, shadow, and diagnostics; persistent context stays flat and native endpoints remain exact.
